name: 169. A duplicate routing rule priority is a 409 conflict (routing-priority-conflict)
description:
Two routing rules in one scope cannot share a priority. The store rejected the second one, but as a plain error the API answered 500 "Failed to create routing rule" (or "Failed to update routing rule in database"), which reads as a server failure a client may retry, and for a rule scoped to a team, customer or virtual key the message printed the address of the scope ID's pointer instead of the ID. The conflict is now ErrAlreadyExists, answered 409 with the priority and scope ID spelled out.

(1) A global rule at a priority already taken is a 409 naming the priority, and moving another rule onto it with PUT is a 409 too. (2) A virtual-key-scoped duplicate is a 409 whose message names the virtual key's ID. Every rule matches only a header no request sends and is deleted by its row. Run with FEATURE="routing-priority-conflict".
